rationale: Clinical penetrance data for epilepsy/seizures in GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder (NEDFABS) differ substantially depending on the cohort and ascertainment strategy. In the cohort described by Abdel-Hamid et al. (2025), ascertained via GeneMatcher for neurodevelopmental features, seizures were documented in only 2 of 4 (50%) individuals. In contrast, the cohort described by De Hayr et al. (2025) identified seizures in the vast majority of their cohort (11 of 12 individuals, ~92%), consistent with early descriptions emerging from epileptic encephalopathy screening pipelines (Papuc et al., 2019). Aggregated across published cases (13 of 16, ~81%), the penetrance sits directly on the boundary between incomplete penetrance (50-75%) and a near-obligatory hallmark (>80%), producing an active conflict between ascertainment series.

evidence.text: In a cohort of four individuals from three unrelated families with biallelic GTF3C3 variants identified through GeneMatcher, clinical seizures were explicitly recorded in only 50% of the individuals.

conflicts: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2025) observed seizures in only 2 of 4 (50%) individuals in a general neurodevelopmental GeneMatcher cohort, whereas De Hayr et al. (2025) reported seizures in 11 of 12 (91.7%) individuals in an independent cohort, leaving the true non-biased penetrance undetermined.

new_directions.question_text: Does seizure onset in GTF3C3-related NEDFABS correlate with specific variant classes, such as missense loss-of-function versus truncating or splice-disrupting alleles?
new_directions.rationale: De Hayr et al. predominantly characterized recurrent missense and splice-altering alleles (p.Ala168Val, p.Leu423Pro, p.Arg807Cys/His) with high seizure incidence, whereas Abdel-Hamid et al. observed nonsense and different missense variants with 50% seizure presence.

new_directions.question_text: Is the observed lower seizure penetrance in some GTF3C3 cohorts age-dependent, reflecting late-onset epilepsy that has not yet manifested in younger pediatric cases?
new_directions.rationale: Longitudinal follow-up of unaffected pediatric individuals is required to establish whether seizure absence is permanent or simply reflects evaluation prior to the typical age of onset.
